records.judge_reason: The report closely mirrors the labelled themes. The configuration and file-discovery, line-splitting, comments/pragmas and string-processing/preview groups are nearly identical. duplicates.reason: Same root cause: an old lock-file pin on a closely tied package (torchvision->torch, dagster-k8s->dagster) is kept and blocks a version change in the input, causing ResolutionImpossible unless --upgrade or -P is used.
Same failure: an old pytest-httpx pin (requires httpx==0.25.*) is kept and conflicts with the new httpx==0.24.1 requirement instead of being dropped; a commenter links the two issues.

top_issues.reason: Confirmed regression since 7.6.1: the JSON API URL lost /pypi/, so --generate-hashes silently downloads every file (GiBs); also affects Dependabot; a one-line fix was supplied.
Regression since 6.10.0: pip-compile hangs when its input is a named pipe because it reads the input twice.
Common resolver failure, reported three times (#2114, #1997): old pins are not dropped when they conflict, so users fall back to a full --upgrade.
After leaving Jazzband the project needs a security reporting policy; GitHub private reporting is already on but the policy text still needs drafting.
pip-sync --python-executable evaluates markers for the wrong environment, which can silently install the wrong packages.

records.judge_reason: Most report themes line up with labelled ones. Resolver, hashes/caching, pip-sync, maintenance/CI and packaging standards all match closely. The 'Packaging standards' theme becomes a catch-all for unrelated feature requests: #1804, #2000, #2173, #2069, #2010, #2151, #1850 and #2172. Some issues are misplaced: #2125 (pip-args/config) sits in hashes, #2123 in pip-sync, #2135 in CLI, and #2047 in resolver. Several issues are missing, including #2160, #2170, #2096, #1836, #1873 and #1831. Mostly sound, but with a vague catch-all theme and some misplacements.

records.judge_reason: The report matches several labelled themes: pip-sync, maintenance/CI/docs and resolver are largely intact. Elsewhere the groupings drift. Some of its issues go to 'Error messages', while header and output feature requests (#2247, #2064, #1876, #2051, #1804) land in a catch-all 'New features and packaging standards'. That catch-all lumps PEP work together with unrelated feature requests such as #2155, #2464, #2000, #2123 and #1850. The caching/concurrency theme is reasonably coherent, but it includes the CI-pinning issue #2404. records.judge_reason:

records.judge_reason: The report broadly follows the labelled structure. 'Wrong reading for one character or word' closely matches the labelled wrong-readings theme. It adds #284, #249 and #221: #249 is plausibly a reading error, while #221 fits better under tones. 'Wrong word splitting' matches the heteronyms theme, though it omits #133, #362 and #249. 'Neutral tone' matches tones, though #144 (erhua) fits only loosely and #221 is missing. The 'obscure readings' theme mixes reading complaints (#321, #293, #263) with data-source issues (#43, #342) and an accuracy evaluation (#133), so it is incoherent. 'Feature requests' is a vague catch-all that merges romanisation and output formats with shell completion, input-method import and pinyin-to-hanzi conversion. 'Versions in other languages' is coherent but small. Several themes match, but some are vague or mix unrelated issues.

records.judge_reason: The report gets several themes right. The tones theme matches the labelled one closely; it adds erhua (#144), which is defensible. The other-language ports (#233, #212) form a coherent small group. The specific wrong-readings theme mostly matches, but it also absorbs the heteronym and segmentation issues #344, #302 and #286. Splitting out surname readings (#297, #120) is a fine, coherent subtheme. The 'rare/archaic readings and data sources' theme mixes unrelated issues: it puts wrong-reading reports (#321, #263) alongside a data-source promotion (#342), a dictionary collaboration (#43) and an accuracy evaluation (#133). records.judge_reason: The report's five themes line up closely with the five labelled themes, and each is a coherent, distinct topic. A few issues are placed differently. #249 and #263 are swapped between the wrong-reading theme and the context/heteronym theme; either placement is defensible. #284 moved to wrong readings and #144 (erhua) moved to tones, both reasonable. #362 (importing input-method dictionaries) moved to feature requests, which fits reasonably. #307 (shell completion) and #184 (pinyin-to-hanzi) also moved to feature requests, which is plausible. The 'Feature and interface requests' theme is somewhat broader and vaguer than the labelled 'romanisation styles and output formats', since it mixes formatting requests with unrelated features like shell completion and reverse conversion. Overall the groupings are mostly the same, with a few misplacements and one broader catch-all theme.
